Subject: Query: separating control plane responsibilities for our on‑prem deployment

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for last week's demo. We're preparing our internal network team brief and had a few concrete asks about splitting responsibilities across control plane (k8s + control APIs) and the on‑prem data plane (inference nodes):

1) We want a minimal demarcation diagram that shows who owns TLS termination, cert rotation, and egress filtering for inference telemetry.
2) Can you confirm if the control plane needs outbound access to the customer's internet or only to internal registries and Redwood's control plane endpoints?
3) For disaster scenarios, what failover behaviors do you recommend for the data plane when control-plane connectivity degrades?

We're aiming to have a single slide for our security review on Monday (Jun 22). If you have a short playbook or reference diagram you can share that would be ideal.

Best,
Samir
Network Security Lead | Vertex Cloud

Hi Samir / Anna —

Thanks — great questions. I've attached a compact schematic (segregated-controlplane-dataflow_v1.drawio.png) and a short extract from our private deployment runbook that addresses TLS/cert rotation and egress expectations. Highlights below:

- TLS & certs: Customer owns edge TLS termination for tenant ingress and any on‑prem NATs; Redwood recommends using mutual TLS for control‑plane RPCs between the private control plane agent and Redwood control endpoints. Certificate rotation is supported via your KMS; we provide a CSR + signed cert flow or can integrate with your ACME pipeline.
- Egress & registries: Control plane requires outbound access only to Redwood control endpoints and (optionally) package registries for image pulls. Images can be pre‑staged in a local registry to avoid outbound egress.
- Telemetry & logs: We stream agent telemetry to a customer‑owned aggregator if preferred; otherwise, telemetry can be proxied through the customer's egress with strict allowlist rules.
- Failover behavior: Data plane (inference pods) will continue serving cached model shards for short control‑plane outages. For extended offline windows, we recommend a degraded mode policy: 1) serve on‑host cached models, 2) restrict new model load/rollouts, 3) revert to a pinned model snapshot.

I've also included a short decision table in the attach that maps responsibilities by component. If useful, we can convert the draw.io into a one‑page slide for your Monday review.

Next steps:
- I'll loop in Jonas for the operational handoff checklist and Kim for KMS/cert integration notes.
- If you want a concise one‑pager for security, say so and we'll produce it today.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Solutions | Redwood Inference

Samir — quick operational notes to supplement Marissa's summary:

- Control‑plane outbound endpoints: minimal list attached to the runbook extract (IP/CIDR + FQDN); if you prefer registry isolation we can provide an image bundle and a signed OCI artifact that your air‑gap process can import.
- Cert rotation: our agent supports automated rotation on a configurable cadence; ops will need a service account with CSR signing permissions if you want us to manage rotation end‑to‑end.
- Egress filtering for telemetry: recommend an allowlist for 3 FQDNs (telemetry, metrics ingest, control API). We support TLS termination at the edge and will never require plaintext egress.
- Failover: add two items to your runbook: (a) a cache eviction threshold (we recommend >2GB free per node), (b) a manual rollback play to a pinned model. We'll provide a small script to check cache/kv health and report to your monitoring.

Action items for Redwood:
- Provide one‑page slide by EOD Thu (we'll convert draw.io) — owners: marissa/jonas.
- Share sample service account policy for CSR-based rotation — owner: kimberly.

Jonas
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
